events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We have reviewed your dispute: part of the fare is refunded. You will receive $4.05 as a Ryde voucher. The decision follows Ryde's dispute policy and the trip record.

DRIVER: We reviewed the trip and the fare has been adjusted. The detour between 2:10pm and 2:15pm is excused because of the accident reported on the usual route. The loop between 2:17pm and 2:29pm is not: the rider's "sure" only covered the road you named, and the 7-Eleven stop did not authorise that route, since you chose the Beach Road store without telling the rider first. $4.05 is refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher. No account flag applies to you.

ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $4.05 voucher to the rider for the unexempted 2.87 km on the 14:17–14:29 segment; retain the $1.08 meter waiting charge and the rest of the metered fare. + flag_account (demo text)
ruling.reasoning:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the fare moves with distance and the excess kilometres of any unexempted off-route segment enter the meter [F1][F6][RD-2]. The per-km rate is taken from this trip's own fare record as distance fare ÷ distance km: $13.55 ÷ 9.61 km = $1.4100/km, which matches the $7.99 excess line (5.67 km × $1.4100) [F6][F9][RD-2].

Segment 1 (14:10–14:15, +1.85 km) [F4]: the driver asked "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" at 14:01 [F10] and the rider answered "Sure." at 14:02 [F11], i.e. before the segment started at 14:10 [F4][F13]. The trace records an LTA accident reported at 13:52, 0 m from the optimal route and inside this segment's window, on the substituted stretch [F18], corroborated by ORCHARD ROAD speed band 1 (0–9 km/h) over 14:00–14:10 [F15]. RD-4 therefore exempts this segment independently of the consent question [F4][F18][F15][RD-4], and I do not need to decide the RD-5 scope point for it. Segments are assessed one by one under RD-1, so the driver's "one continuous diversion" reading does not carry segment 1's excuse over to segment 2.

Segment 2 (14:17–14:29, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off route, containing the 4 min 10 s stationary period at (1.3025, 103.8638), 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off) [F5][F2]: no RD-4 incident qualifies — the only incident (F18) is tied to the Orchard Road stretch, and speed-band evidence cannot exempt on its own [F5][F18][F17][RD-4]. On RD-5, the rider's only pre-segment messages are "Sure." and "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?" [F11], both sent before 14:17 but neither agreeing to this loop. "Sure" attaches to the driver's named-road proposal (Cavenagh) [F10][F11]; even on the driver's own reading that is a named-road authorisation, and the record places this segment somewhere else — the driver's own statement says he chose and drove to "the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road" [F14] — so an agreement to Cavenagh does not cover it: this branch counts, not undetermined [F5][F11][F14][RD-5]. The verbal-agreement assertion in the driver's statement is not consent [F14][RD-5].

On RD-3, the rider's "Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way" named no place [F11]; the driver alone picked the Beach Road store and did not tell the rider that location before driving there, and the choice pushed the track into this off-route segment [F2][F5][F14], so RD-3(b) applies and the extra kilometres are not excused by the stop request — the segment counts [F5][F14][RD-3].

Amount [F5][F6][RD-2]: 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.0467 → $4.05. The waiting charge $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) is RydeTAXI meter waiting time for the rider-requested stop and is not refunded [F2][F7][F11][RD-3]; the remaining excess (F1's +5.7 km against the 3.9 km optimal route, and miles not assigned to any segment) is not refunded under RD-2 [F1][F6][RD-2].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile shows 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days, so this case does not make the breach "repeated" and no account flag attaches [F21][RD-6]; the rider asked for no flag [F20]. The trace marks this ✗, settled by code.

Safety screen: I read the complaint, the three chat messages (F10–F12), the driver's statement (F14) and the traffic facts — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the tone is a route/fare argument only [F10][F11][F12][F14][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence: the chat record is complete with all three messages timestamped [F13], the segments are measured [F4][F5], the fare line items are recorded [F6][F7][F9], and the RD-4 incident screen is settled (F4 ✓, F5 ✗) [F18], so nothing element-needing is missing; the observations do not change the amount and are classified "counts" on the record, which is decidable either way [F11][F14][RD-5][RD-3].

rejected_claims.reason: Partly rejected as far as it is used to deny segment 1's excuse: F18 (accident 0 m from the optimal route, reported 13:52) and F15 (ORCHARD ROAD band 1, 14:00–14:10) satisfy RD-4(a) for the 14:10–14:15 segment [F18][F15][F4][RD-4]. Accepted only as to segment 2, where no incident qualifies [F5][F18][RD-4].

Accepted as far as it goes but the underlying point is wrong on the facts: F21 shows a prior upheld dispute (route: 0, no-show: 1), so route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 and RD-6's flag condition is not met [F21][RD-6]; this does not, however, prevent the RD-2 refund the rider seeks.

Rejected as to segment 2: F14 places the segment at a stop the driver chose on Beach Road, so the 14:02 'Sure.' to the Cavenagh proposal [F10][F11][F14] does not cover it under RD-5 (specific named-road/area consent does not cover a driver-chosen location elsewhere, and a verbal-agreement claim in the driver's statement is not consent) [F14][F5][RD-5].
Rejected as to segment 2: F18 is an incident on the optimal Orchard Road stretch used for segment 1 (trace: 0 m, inside F4's window); it says nothing about the 14:17–14:29 loop [F18][F4][F5][RD-4].

Rejected as to segment 2: F15 and F16 cover at most 14:00–14:10/14:00–14:35 on Orchard and Bras Basah Road and cannot themselves exempt, the trace marking RD-4(b) as corroboration only and speed band alone as non-exempting for F5 [F15][F16][F17][F5][RD-4].

Rejected as an attempt to keep the billed excess in place: D7 concedes the +5.7 km against the 3.9 km optimal route and the 26.5 min against a 7.7 min estimate [F1][F3][F6], so the residue of the $7.99 beyond the segments is a further breach of the shortest-and-most-direct duty under RD-1 [F1][F6][RD-1][RD-2].

The rider also agreed at 14:02 to the driver's 14:01 Cavenagh proposal, before the segment start [F10][F11][F13][RD-5], but the RD-4 reasonable-cause branch alone exempts this segment, so I need not decide the RD-5 scope point here.

RD-3(b)/RD-5: the rider asked only for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' without naming any place [F11]; the driver's own post-trip statement says he chose and drove to 'the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road', a location he did not tell the rider before driving there, and that choice produced this off-route segment with the 4 min 10 s stop 2098 m from the drop-off [F14][F2][F5]. No qualifying RD-4 incident covers it [F18][F17][RD-4], and the only pre-segment rider messages, 'Sure.' to the Cavenagh proposal and the unnamed stop request, do not cover a driver-chosen stop away from that road [F11][F14][RD-5]. The extra kilometres are therefore unexempted and refundable at the metered rate [F5][F6][RD-2].

certificate: ✓ RD-1 off-route segment(s) exist [case] 2 segment(s) (F4, F5)
✓ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F4] incident within 300 m of optimal km 0.8–1.6 (F18)
– RD-5 consent scope [F4] not needed: RD-4 already exempts this segment (no evidence)
– RD-3 rider-requested stop [F4] not needed: RD-4 already exempts this segment (no evidence)
✗ RD-4 (a) incident on the replaced stretch, reported before the detour [F5] no qualifying incident (speed band alone does not exempt) (F18)

? RD-5 rider agreed to this route before the detour; scope of that agreement [F5] RULE: exempt only if a RIDER message sent before 14:17:45 agrees AND the agreement covers this segment. Three kinds of agreement: (1) GENERAL route choice ('take whichever way is faster') covers a route chosen to get there, not an errand of the driver's own (a stop away from the route, a loop that reaches nothing: counts). (2) A SPECIFIC named road or area ('go round via X') covers driving on X only: the record must tie this segment to X (a stop on X, a message placing the car on X, a road name in a fact); timing alone does not, and the fact table carries no road names for the driven path — if nothing ties them, the finding is undetermined (G13); if the record places this segment somewhere else (a stop away from X, the driver's own statement naming another road or place, a stop the driver chose the location of), the agreement to X does not cover it: counts. (3) Scope unclear: undetermined. A driver's claim of agreement that appears only in his statement is not consent (G11); a complete chat record with no rider agreement before the segment: counts. This finding changes the amount. Evidence — F10: Chat #1 14:01 driver: “Hi, traffic on Orchard is bad, ok if I go round by Cavenagh?”; F11: Chat #2 14:02 rider: “Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?”; F12: Chat #3 14:03 driver: “Ok”; F14: Driver statement (written after the trip, not part of the chat): “Orchard was jammed after an accident, rider agreed to go round by Cavenagh and asked for a stop. I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road.” (F10, F11, F12, F14)

? RD-3 rider-requested stop; whether the rider named this place [F5] RULE (RD-3(a)): exempt if a RIDER message before the segment named a specific place and the car stopped there (the whole way there is exempt; how long the stop lasted or how far the place was does not reduce it). A stop the rider asked for without naming a place ('a 7-Eleven on the way') does not excuse the driver's choice of a far one → counts. Stops in this segment: F2. (F10, F11, F12, F2)
✗ RD-6 prior upheld route dispute in 90 d (repeated breach → flag_account) [case] route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 (F21)

? SAFE-1 safety screen: any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation in the chat, statement or complaint [case] answer in safety_concern (none / suspected / confirmed) with safety_basis; suspected or confirmed → escalate. no hint word; read the messages anyway, a threat needs no keyword (no evidence)
allowed outcomes: refund_partial, no_action, escalate; amount = Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × $1.4100/km (distance_fare ÷ distance_km), rounded to cents
flag_account required: False

what_would_change: F5: the judge found no rider agreement covering this segment, so $4.05 is refunded; a rider message agreeing to it before it started would have exempted it.
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.

claims.assertion: Segment 1 (14:10–14:15, 2.68 km driven vs 0.83 km optimal, +1.85 km) is the Cavenagh Road loop the driver proposed in Chat #1 at 14:01 and the rider accepted in Chat #2 at 14:02, i.e. before the segment started at 14:10; the rider's message is a general route authorisation ('Sure') for the faster way, so this segment is excused.

Segment 2 (14:17–14:29, 3.64 km driven vs 0.77 km optimal, +2.87 km, up to 1553 m off route) coincides with the stationary 4 min 10 s at (1.3025, 103.8638), 2995 m from pickup and 2098 m from drop-off, and no rider message before 14:17 asked for that detour — the rider in Chat #2 asked for 'a 7-Eleven on the way', not for a run out to Beach Road.

The Beach Road 7-Eleven the driver admits choosing (driver statement: 'I stopped at the 7-Eleven I know on Beach Road') was the driver's own pick of a stop that pushed the track into an off-route segment, and he did not tell the rider that location before driving there, so the extra kilometres of segment 2 are not excused by the rider's stop request.

The driver's claim of an accident-related jam is only partly corroborated: the accident fact sits 0 m from the optimal route and is reported 13:52 before the trip, but it concerns Orchard Road towards Bras Basah, and an LTA record cannot be read to excuse a 2.87 km deviation with a 4-minute stop 2.1 km from the destination.

This is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the unexcused segment 2 extra kilometres entered the meter: the excess distance billed was $7.99 (5.67 km × $1.4100/km, the trip's distance fare ÷ distance km), and the rider is entitled to the portion attributable to that 2.87 km.

Waiting time was billed $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) for the rider-requested 7-Eleven stop; a stop the rider asked for at meter waiting units is chargeable on RydeTAXI, so no refund is sought for the $1.08.
The driver has 3 disputes and 1 upheld (no-show) in the last 90 days, but no route dispute upheld, so RD-6's 'repeated route offence' flag is not triggered and none is requested.

weaknesses: The rider's own Chat #2 message 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' plus the driver's 'Ok' in F12 can be read as a rider-named/requested stop, which under RD-3(a) would put the beach-side stop outside the detour analysis; the counter is that no location was named and F14 shows the driver chose the Beach Road store, invoking RD-3(b).

Segment 1 sits between two strong system records the driver will rely on — the accident at 0 m from the optimal route reported at 13:52 (F18) and Orchard Road speed band 1 during 14:00–14:10 (F15) — so the driver will argue RD-4 excuses both segments, not just segment 1, and may also argue the two segments are one continuous diversion.

The $4.05 figure is computed from F5's 2.87 km × the F6 per-km rate rather than from a fare fact that itself isolates segment 2; if the judge treats F6's $7.99 (5.67 km, which exceeds the 4.72 km sum of the two segments, cf. F1) as a single divisible pool, the allocation argument falls back on the per-km rate, which the driver can dispute.

Part of segment 2's elapsed time includes the 4 min 10 s stationary period (F2) that the rider asked to stop for, so the driver may argue the rider consented to the diversion in substance even if not to Beach Road specifically (a verbal-agreement claim that RD-5/G11 rejects when only in the driver's statement, F14).

The rider filed the complaint as an 'overcharge' (F6/F9) but the fare facts show no hidden or unpublished add-on, so if the refund argument is framed as an overcharge it fails; it must be framed as RD-2 metered-distance refund, which is a narrow recovery of at most a few dollars.

claims.assertion: RydeTAXI meters by distance, so the disputed amount is limited to the metered km; the fare facts show the per-km rate used for this trip is $1.4100/km, so any refund on an unexempted segment is extra_km × $1.4100 (F6, F9).

Segment 14:10-14:15 (F4) is covered by the rider's own general route authorisation: the driver asked before leaving the optimal route at 14:01 'ok if I go round by Cavenagh?' and the rider answered at 14:02 'Sure. Can you stop at a 7-Eleven on the way?' (F10, F11, F13).

That segment is additionally justified as a reasonable cause: an LTA-reported accident at 13:52 blocked two lanes on the optimal route ('Accident on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed'), 0 m from the optimal route, i.e. on the substituted stretch (F18), and it falls inside the segment window (F4).

The accident report is corroborated by the rider's direction of travel: ORCHARD ROAD was at speed band 1 (0-9 km/h) during 14:00-14:10 while the accepted Cavenagh route ran at band 4 on Bras Basah Road, so the route taken was the faster one for that stretch (F15, F16).

We do not contest segment 14:17-14:29 (F5) downward: the 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20-14:24 (F2) is the 7-Eleven stop the rider asked for (F11), but the record contains no rider message naming 7-Eleven on Beach Road, so the extra 2.87 km on that segment is not exempt and must be returned at the metered rate.
The refund is therefore 2.87 km × $1.4100/km = $4.05, being the excess distance on the unexempted segment only (F5, F6).

The remaining +2.83 km of the +5.7 km excess (F1) is the driver's own account error and is not charged to the rider: the $7.99 excess shown as billed (F6) is a figure from the trip's own distance fare, which this case does not ask to preserve beyond the formula above (F1, F6).

The 4 min 10 s stop generated a waiting charge of $1.08 (F2, F7), lawfully charged as RydeTAXI meter waiting time, and the rider's complaint is only about route and overcharging, not the waiting charge (F2, F7).
No account flag is warranted on this record: the driver's profile shows 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days (F21), so RD-6's 'repeated route offender' condition is not met.

weaknesses: Segment F5 is the driver's real exposure: the rider asked only for 'a 7-Eleven on the way' (F11) with no place named, the driver's statement says he chose the Beach Road 7-Eleven (F14), and no fact ties the 14:17-14:29 loop (F5) to any rider-named place - so the extra 2.87 km is unfunded and RD-2 refund of $4.05 is likely owed.

The 'Cavenagh' consent (F10, F11) is a named-road authorisation and nothing in the record ties the 14:10-14:15 driving to Cavenagh Road itself (F4); on a strict RD-5/G13 reading the rider's advocate will argue that segment is undetermined or unexempted rather than consented, which would add up to 1.85 km × $1.4100 = $2.61 to the refund.

The scale of the overall detour is hard to defend in tone if not in law: 9.6 km vs 3.9 km optimal (F1), a 26.5 min trip vs 7.7 min estimated (F3), and both off-route windows (F4, F5) start at 14:10, just minutes after pickup at 14:05, which invites the rider's 'I never asked for Beach Road' complaint (F11 vs F14).

The rider's profile is clean (610-day account, 4.9 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days, F20), so the rider's advocate will present the complaint as good-faith and RD-6's account-flag risk will be argued to attach to the driver instead.

points.response: Agreed: this is a RydeTAXI trip and the excess distance billed is $7.99 at 5.67 km × $1.4100/km, so the per-km rate is $1.4100 and any refund is extra_km × $1.4100.

Conceded on segment 1 only and only as a general authorisation: the rider's 14:02 'Sure' (F11) followed the driver's 14:01 proposal (F10), both before the 14:10 segment start, but it permits a faster way to the destination, not a 4 min 10 s stop 2.1 km from the drop-off; the driver's own G13-style gap (nothing ties F4 to Cavenagh Road) is his burden, not the rider's, so the rider does not press segment 1.

The LTA accident at 13:52 was 0 m from the optimal route but is described as 'on Orchard Road (towards Bras Basah) after Cavenagh Road, two lanes closed' (F18), i.e. it corroborates the 14:10–14:15 Cavenagh loop the rider accepted, not the 14:17–14:29 loop out to (1.3025, 103.8638); and traffic band evidence cannot stand alone under RD-4.

The band-1 Orchard Road reading covers 14:00–14:10 and the band-4 Bras Basah Road reading 14:00–14:35, so both corroborate the first segment at most; nothing in the traffic facts either explains the 2.87 km addition of segment 2 or puts an incident on the substituted stretch of that segment.

Conceded: the driver admits the 2.87 km on the 14:17–14:29 segment is unfunded, no rider message before that segment named any place, the driver chose the Beach Road 7-Eleven himself (F14), so RD-3(b) applies and the segment is unexcused.
